The first 14 days matter most

What to do after a Florida car accident

  1. 01

    See a doctor within 14 days

    Florida's PIP law requires care within 14 days to keep your benefits — even if you feel fine.

  2. 02

    Document everything

    Photos of the scene, damage, and injuries. Get the police report number and the other driver's insurance.

  3. 03

    Don't talk to their insurer

    The other driver's insurer may call quickly. You're not required to give a statement — let an attorney handle it.

  4. 04

    Call before you settle

    Early offers are often far below what a claim is worth. A free review shows where you stand.

Good to know

Common questions

How much does it cost to hire you?+

Nothing upfront. We work on contingency — paid only if we win. The review is always free.

I already feel fine — do I still need a doctor?+

Yes. Injuries like whiplash appear days later, and Florida requires care within 14 days for PIP.

The insurance company already called me. What do I say?+

You don't have to give a recorded statement. Talk to an attorney first.

How long do I have to file a claim in Florida?+

Usually 2 years for crashes on/after March 24, 2023. Some are shorter — don't wait.

What if the accident was partly my fault?+

Often yes. Florida uses comparative negligence. A quick review tells you where you stand.
